item.title: Children’s Mental Health Week - SOS Children's Villages
item.description: On Children's Mental Health Week, we highlight how for too many children, the world's marked by fear, loss and uncertainty. Together we can change this.

item.title: Family-like care in Uganda: Leo’s story - SOS Children's Villages
item.description: After losing his parents at just five years old, and his grandparents becoming unable to care for him, Leo joined a family at SOS Children's Villages Uganda. Now 16, Leo reflects on the profound effect the care he received has had on him and how it's shaped the person he's become.

item.title: Our commitment to cyber security: Cyber Essentials Plus certified - SOS Children's Villages
item.description: SOS Children's Villages UK are now Cyber Essentials Plus certified, demonstrating our commitment to excellence in data and cyber security and safeguarding.

item.title: Four years of war in Ukraine: the impact on children and families - SOS Children's Villages
item.description: Four years of war in Ukraine have left freezing homes, power cuts, and damaged infrastructure as part of everyday life for millions of children and families.

item.title: Future developments at SOS Children’s Villages UK - SOS Children's Villages
item.description: Supporting our local partners to deliver change in 2026 and beyond

item.title: Two years on: Children evacuated from Gaza face renewed uncertainty - SOS Children's Villages
item.description: As violence escalates in the Middle East, children evacuated from Gaza face renewed uncertainty and trauma.

item.title: Across the distance: Making ma’amoul with my mother - SOS Children's Villages
item.description: A reflection on family, tradition and staying connected between Ramallah and the UK by Lina Salameh.

item.title: Albina’s story: Surviving loss and rebuilding strength - SOS Children's Villages
item.description: On 2 November 2024, a Russian shelling attack on the Zelenivka village in the Kherson region in Ukraine, brought tragedy to many families. Among those affected was 17-year-old Albina.

item.title: Restoring hope and livelihoods: The journey of Daahiro Abdulle - SOS Children's Villages
item.description: Elasha Biyaha, an informal settlement on the outskirts of Mogadishu in Somalia, is home to families rebuilding their lives after drought and conflict forced them to leave everything behind. Among them is 72-year-old Daahiro Abdulle, a grandmother whose life has been shaped by grief, loss, and resilience.

item.title: Three years on: Sudan’s crisis and the risk of a lost generation - SOS Children's Villages
item.description: Three years into the conflict, Sudan continues to face a deepening humanitarian crisis that has disrupted every aspect of life. What began as a sudden escalation has evolved into a prolonged emergency, affecting access to education, health services, protection, and basic needs. Insecurity, disease outbreaks, and rising crime are redefining what safety means for millions.

item.title: Support for widowed mothers in Bolivia: Wilma's story - SOS Children's Villages
item.description: Wilma, a widowed mother in Bolivia, found hope through her children and support through SOS Children’s Villages.

item.title: Youth peer counselling supports mental health - SOS Children's Villages
item.description: Discover how youth peer counselling in Nepal empowers young people like Sabita to support each other’s mental health and overcome stigma.

item.title: Mental health in Bangladesh: Arsha’s journey - SOS Children's Villages
item.description: Childhood trauma affects so many globally. Discover how mental health in Bangladesh is being addressed through care and counselling.
